bands.1:
You have won Poet Pip's badge. Now she is on your side.

"Tonight the set is a sleeping dragon," says Pip. "We are mice in its pocket."

"The film crew has gone home," says Indi. "We sneak in."

"Picture it," says Pip.

Indi's disguises are cardboard trees. Mo's label says, "PROP: BUSH (SMALL)."

"I feel a bit bushed," says Mo. Everyone groans.

Gus holds up a green balloon. "The Bogey Bomb! A month of my greenest bogeys. On a green screen, green things vanish on camera."

At the set, Gus pops the balloon. Splat! Everyone is green. On the Goldies' screen, the crew vanishes. Only gumboots are left.

"Floating boots," says a Goldie. "I need a nap."

The set is all fake. There are plastic trees and a paddling pool full of brown water.

A Goldie walks past. Everyone freezes like trees.

"The Reef Rays are losing by ninety," whispers Tully.

"Did that tree just talk?" asks the Goldie. He walks on.

Behind the green screen are tiny cages. The Similoon is in a cage the size of a shoebox.

Zed types PICTUREPERFECTME into a gold cabinet. Inside is an album: "SET PHOTOS. NEVER POST."

The photos show Maxx with a thumbs up. Behind him are the tiny cages.

"That's proof," says Pip.

You put the album in your bag. Wren and Pip open the cages.

Then the lights snap on. Goldies block the door with nets.

"Similoon!" cries Pip. "You are as fierce as a crocodile!"

The Similoon grows into a huge, feathery crocodile. SNAP! The Goldies run into the mud.

On the boat, you look at the last photo. It was taken from Maxx's yacht at night. A giant shape glows under the sea. Maxx has written, "FOUND HER! THE BIG ONE."

It is Old Glimmer, the giant glowing ray. Pip does not say it like a poem. She says it plainly.

"He knows where she is."

It is Old Glimmer, the great glowing ray. Pip stares at it for a long time. Then, for once, she says it plainly.

"He knows where she is."
bands.3:
You have won Poet Pip's badge, and the poet of Mirage Mangroves is finally on your side. She still won't say anything plainly, but at least now she says it to you.

"Tonight the set is a sleeping dragon," she whispers, as the fog machines hum, "and we are the mice in its pocket."

"She means the film crew has gone home," says Indi, "and we're sneaking in."

"Picture it," says Pip.

Indi's disguises are cardboard trees with holes for faces. Each has a label that says "PROP: TREE". Mo's label says "PROP: BUSH (SMALL)".

"I'm not small, I'm compact," says Mo. "But I am feeling a bit bushed." Everyone groans, including several trees.

Gus holds up a wobbling green balloon. "The Bogey Bomb," he whispers. "A whole month of my greenest bogeys. That's not gross. That's science."

"Why do we need bogeys?" asks Tully.

"On a green screen, anything green disappears on camera," says Gus. "So we go green."

At the edge of the set, MaxxCam drones circle slowly, filming everything. Gus pops the Bogey Bomb right above the crew. Splat! Everyone is dripping green. On the Goldies' screen, the whole crew vanishes against the green wall, leaving only a row of gumboots floating along by themselves.

"Floating boots," mutters a Goldie, rubbing his eyes. "I need a nap."

Inside, the set is completely fake. There are plastic mangroves, a paddling pool full of brown water, a painted sunset and a leaf blower labelled "WILD WIND". A clapperboard says, "MAXX BRAVES THE WILD MANGROVES. TAKE 47." The deep, dangerous swamp from the video is knee-deep.

Then a Goldie strolls round the corner. Everyone freezes like trees.

In Tully's pocket, the footy radio crackles. "The Reef Rays are losing by ninety," she whispers.

The Goldie stops. "Did that tree just say ninety?"

"No," says the bush.

The Goldie shrugs and wanders off.

Behind the green screen are rows of tiny cages: Likkabys, Plonketts, Whopskips and a Humbret with its neck bent double. In a cage the size of a shoebox sits the Similoon, trying to be as small as a pea.

Zed types PICTUREPERFECTME into a gold cabinet. Inside is an album: "SET PHOTOS. NEVER, EVER POST."

Every photo shows Maxx grinning beside the green screen, thumb up. Behind him, in every one, are the tiny cages.

"Each cage is a shoebox with a heartbeat," says Pip quietly. Then, plainly: "That's proof."

You slide the album into your bag. Wren and Pip open the cages, and the Similoon unfolds her long neck with a happy honk.

Then the lights snap on. Three Goldies with nets block the only door.

"Similoon!" cries Pip. "You are as fierce as a crocodile!"

The Similoon swells into a huge, feathery crocodile with very fluffy teeth. SNAP! The Goldies scream and sprint straight out into the real mud, where they sink up to their knees.

Back on the boat, you turn to the last photo. It was taken at night, from the deck of a huge yacht. Deep under the sea glows an enormous shape, wider than a footy field. Maxx has circled it in gold pen: "FOUND HER! THE BIG ONE."

It is Old Glimmer, the great glowing ray from the old sea stories. Pip goes very still. No simile comes, and no metaphor. When she speaks at last, it is plainly.

"He knows where she is."
bands.4:
Poet Pip has given you her badge, and with it her trust, though not, it turns out, a single plain sentence.

"Tonight the set is a sleeping dragon," she whispers, as the fog machines hum somewhere in the mist, "and we are the mice in its pocket."

"The film crew's gone home," Indi translates. "We sneak in."

"Picture it," says Pip.

Indi's disguise of the Chapter is a small forest of cardboard trees, with holes cut out for faces and a label on each that says "PROP: TREE". Mo's label, for reasons Indi refuses to explain, says "PROP: BUSH (SMALL)".

"I'm not small, I'm compact," says Mo. "Although I am feeling a bit bushed." Several trees groan.

Gus holds up a wobbling green balloon, a month of his greenest bogeys sealed inside. "On a green screen," he explains, "anything green vanishes on camera."

At the edge of the set, MaxxCam drones circle slowly. Gus pops the Bogey Bomb directly above the crew, and everyone is suddenly dripping green from head to gumboot. On the Goldies' security screen, the whole crew melts into the glowing wall, leaving only a row of gumboots strolling along by themselves.

"Floating boots," mutters a Goldie, rubbing his eyes. "I definitely need a nap."

Inside, the wild swamp from Maxx's videos turns out to be a paddling pool of brown water, surrounded by plastic mangroves, a painted sunset and a leaf blower labelled "WILD WIND". On a folding chair lies a clapperboard: "MAXX BRAVES THE WILD MANGROVES. TAKE 47." Forty-six times, apparently, Maxx was not quite brave enough.

A Goldie strolls round the corner, and the forest freezes.

In Tully's pocket, the footy radio crackles. "The Reef Rays are losing by ninety," she breathes, before she can stop herself.

The Goldie stops. "Did that tree just say ninety?"

"No," says the bush.

The Goldie shrugs and wanders off, muttering about the heat.

Behind the green screen, in rows, are the tiny cages: Likkabys, Plonketts, Whopskips and a Humbret with its long neck bent double. In one the size of a shoebox sits the Similoon, trying very hard to be as small as a pea, because that is the only comparison anyone has made near her all week.

Zed types PICTUREPERFECTME into a gold filing cabinet, and a drawer slides open. Inside is a gold album: "SET PHOTOS. NEVER, EVER POST. STAY GOLD!"

In every photo, Maxx grins beside the green screen, thumb up, teeth blazing. In every photo, just behind his shoulder, are the cages. He never once looks round at them.

"Each cage is a shoebox with a heartbeat," says Pip, and then, more quietly, "That's proof."

You slide the album into your bag. Wren and Pip work along the rows, and when the Similoon's door swings open, she unfolds her long grey neck with a honk so happy that the Plonketts start plonking.

Then the lights snap on. Three Goldies with nets block the only door.

"Similoon!" cries Pip. "You are as fierce as a crocodile!"

The Similoon swells into a huge, feathery crocodile with very fluffy teeth. SNAP! Dropping their nets, the Goldies sprint straight out into the real mud, where, unlike in the videos, the swamp is waist-deep.

Back on the Soggy Biscuit, still faintly green, you turn to the last photo in the album. It was taken at night from the deck of an enormous yacht, looking down. Far below the surface glows a vast shape, wider than a footy field, its edges rippling like a cape in slow wind. Maxx has circled it in gold pen: "FOUND HER! THE BIG ONE. Finale set: need a MUCH bigger green screen."

It is Old Glimmer, the great glowing ray of the old sea stories, and Maxx has not drawn her. He has photographed her, from his own deck.

Pip looks at the photo for a long time. No simile comes, and no metaphor. When she finally speaks, it is in the plainest voice you have ever heard her use, and that frightens you more than anything in the swamp.

"He knows where she is."
